messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: High p95 observed for /v1/generate across inference-prod pool. Alert threshold breached at 2025-11-03T10:13:00Z. Affected hosts: gpu-02,gpu-03,gpu-07.
anna (oncall): I'm oncall, ack. Looking at dashboards now. p50 looks fine, p95 jumped ~10x.
mike (eng-sre): grabbing node logs and perf counters. attaching quick dmesg tail for gpu-03: 
```
[Nov  3 10:13:05] kernel: Out-of-memory: Kill process 4123 (someprocess) score 500 or sacrifice child
[Nov  3 10:13:06] kernel: kernel: major page fault rate spike: task=runtime pid=4210 comm=llama2
[Nov  3 10:13:07] kernel: page allocation failure: order:0, mode:0x20
```
jess (infra): FYI - we deployed a kernel security patch (6.2.15) to that node pool at ~10:10 UTC to address a NIC driver regression. Rollout was staggered but gpu-02/03 had it.
leo (eng-runtime): Traces for the slow requests show long syscall durations (~800-1200ms) inside memcpy and mm_fault handling. Example trace span: 
```
span: request/1234 -> runtime/exec -> syscall:handle_page_fault (duration 973ms)
```
leo (eng-runtime): Also seeing KV cache miss rate spike for those traces — could be correlated but syscall/sys overhead looks primary.
sam (support): Two customers (org-7, org-19) reported timeouts around 10:15 UTC, escalating. No 5xx increase, mostly timeouts and client-side retries.
anna (oncall): Immediate mitigation plan: 1) cordon gpu-03 2) migrate in-flight tasks off gpu-03 3) bounce runtime on remaining nodes to clear any stuck page caches. Starting cordon now.
jess (infra): Cordon started on gpu-03 (kubectl cordon). Eviction of pods in progress; ETA ~8-12 minutes for graceful drain for heavy workloads.
mike (eng-sre): Captured perf counters across nodes pre/post spike: 
```
node gpu-03 (10:09 -> 10:15): context_switches: 1.2M -> 4.0M, major_page_faults: 120 -> 1800, irq/softirq persec up 2x
node gpu-07 (10:09 -> 10:15): context_switches: 0.9M -> 1.0M, major_page_faults: 15 -> 40
```
mike (eng-sre): Uploading full perf snapshots to https://internal.logs/redwood/incidents/1775559876/ (linked).
leo (eng-runtime): Hypotheses (tracking):
H1: Kernel regression in 6.2.15 causing increased major page faults and long syscall stalls. (weight: high)
H2: Runtime change (recent image) causing memory allocation patterns that provoke page churn under new kernel. (weight: medium)
H3: Workload pattern (larger sequences) triggered cold KV cache and heavier page activity coincidentally. (weight: low)
anna (oncall): Triage notes: p50 unchanged -> suggests tail and system-level regression rather than model compute change. Prioritize H1.
jess (infra): Can rollback kernel on gpu-03 but it will require reboot (~10-12m) and reimage if fails. We prefer draining and keeping node offline until we confirm. Rolling rollback to other nodes not recommended until root cause is clear.
mike (eng-sre): For RCA we need: 1) full dmesg from 09:50-10:30 2) perf counter dumps 3) runtime logs with full stack traces for requests hitting page faults. I've pinned these in the log bundle.
leo (eng-runtime): I'm extracting a trace bundle for three p95 traces and linking to the bundle. Key observation: stack shows mm_fault -> do_page_fault -> copy_user_enhanced_fast64 -> runtime memcpy. That chain takes the majority of the tail time.
sam (support): Customer impact: org-7 reported 3 timed-out calls; org-19 saw increased latency but no data loss. Notified both that we are investigating and performing mitigations.
anna (oncall): Live mitigation status: gpu-03 cordoned & draining, traffic rebalanced to gpu-02/07; p95 for /v1/generate dropped from ~1.2s -> ~320ms within 6 minutes after drain. Still elevated vs baseline.
mike (eng-sre): New perf snapshot post-drain shows major_page_faults down by ~80% on cluster. Context switches trending down. That supports H1.
jess (infra): Scheduling a controlled rollback test on a single non-prod node with same kernel change to reproduce. Will run regression test pack for memory-heavy requests.
leo (eng-runtime): Next steps for RCA: 1) reproduce on staging with 6.2.15 + runtime image 2025.10.2 2) if reproducible, bisect kernel patches 3) if not, instrument runtime to log memory access patterns.
mike (eng-sre): Recording timeline here for PM/PMs:
- 10:10 UTC: kernel 6.2.15 rollout started to gpu pool (staggered)
- 10:12 UTC: first p95 anomalies on telemetry
- 10:13 UTC: incident-bot page triggered, initial paging
- 10:14 UTC: oncall ack, logs show major page faults on gpu-03
- 10:18 UTC: cordon gpu-03, drain started
- 10:20 UTC: customer reports received
- 10:26 UTC: p95 improved but still elevated; mitigation continues
- 10:40 UTC: cluster perf back to near-baseline after drains

mike (eng-sre): I'm flagging this for SEV2 RCA. Please add notes in the incident doc: https://internal.incidents/1775559876 (postmortem link will be created).
anna (oncall): Thanks team. I'll stay on hand for the next hour to monitor. If infra confirms kernel reproduction on staging, we'll coordinate a planned rollback for prod nodes during low traffic window.
leo (eng-runtime): Adding a quick checklist for postmortem: evidence for H1 (perf + dmesg), repro steps, mitigation timeline, customer impact, and recommended action (hold kernel rollout until kernel vendor fix, or pin kernel).
sam (support): I'll follow up with impacted customers with the mitigation/update and postmortem ETA.
incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Severity: SEV2. Assigned owners: anna (oncall), mike (eng-sre), jess (infra), leo (eng-runtime).
anna (oncall): Closing live triage here, moving to RCA doc. Will paste any additional logs in that doc.
